headings.title: Definition and Scope of Unsafe Abortion in Nigeria
headings.content: Unsafe abortion is defined by the World Health Organization as a procedure for terminating an unwanted pregnancy carried out either by persons lacking the necessary skills or in an environment that does not conform to minimal medical standards, or both. In Nigeria, this issue constitutes a major public health crisis, contributing significantly to maternal morbidity and mortality statistics. Most procedures occur covertly due to societal stigma, leaving young and unmarried girls particularly vulnerable to substandard interventions. National data consistently reveals that clandestine procedures account for a high percentage of maternal deaths nationwide, heavily burdening tertiary and secondary healthcare facilities with emergency admissions.

headings.title: Legal and Socio-Religious Context in Nigeria
headings.content: The legal framework governing pregnancy termination in Nigeria is restrictive, rooted in the Criminal Code (southern states) and the Penal Code (northern states). Under these laws, abortion is generally illegal unless performed to save the pregnant person's life. This criminalization forces women to seek clandestine options. Culturally and religiously, Nigerian society strongly condemns premarital sex and termination of pregnancy, fostering an atmosphere of secrecy. Consequently, victims of botched procedures often delay seeking orthodox medical help out of fear of legal prosecution or social ostracization.

headings.title: Etiology and Contributing Factors
headings.content:
Unwanted or unintended pregnancies form the root cause of unsafe abortions. These occurrences are driven by multiple interconnected factors:
- **Poverty**: Inability to afford or access reliable modern contraceptives.
- **Ignorance**: Widespread gaps in comprehensive sexual education and reproductive health knowledge.
- **Gender Dynamics**: Power imbalances, sexual coercion, and the prevalence of sexual violence.
- **Systemic Failures**: Weak family planning services in primary healthcare centers and stock-outs of essential commodities.

headings.title: Common Methods Used and Associated Pathophysiology
headings.content:
Methods utilized in clandestine terminations vary depending on access, cost, and gestational age. Traditional and unskilled providers frequently employ dangerous mechanical techniques.

| Method Category | Common Examples | Pathophysiological Risk |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mechanical / Instrument** | Knitting needles, cassava sticks, wire | Uterine perforation, internal hemorrhage, visceral injury |
| **Caustic Chemical** | Potassium permanganate, bleach solutions, herbal concoctions | Severe chemical burns, tissue necrosis, systemic toxicity |
| **Pharmacological** | Misoprostol, oxytocin (misused or incorrect doses) | Incomplete abortion, severe uterine rupture, profuse bleeding |

headings.title: Clinical Presentation and Complications
headings.content: Patients presenting to emergency departments following an unsafe abortion typically exhibit classic signs of sepsis, hemorrhage, or trauma. Nurses must be vigilant for symptoms such as lower abdominal pain, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, abnormal bleeding, fever, and signs of hypovolemic shock. Severe complications include septic shock, peritonitis from uterine perforation, acute renal failure, and long-term pelvic inflammatory disease leading to secondary infertility. Recognizing these clinical indicators swiftly can mean the difference between life and death.

headings.title: Nursing Assessment and Diagnosis
headings.content: A systematic nursing assessment is vital for stabilizing emergency abortion complications. The nurse begins with an ABCDE approach to ensure hemodynamic stability, followed by a focused obstetric and gynecological history regarding the last menstrual period, gestational age estimate, and details of the intervention. Physical examination includes vital signs, abdominal palpation for tenderness or guarding, and a gentle speculum examination if indicated. Essential nursing diagnoses often include Acute Pain, Risk for Infection, Deficient Fluid Volume, and Anxiety.

headings.title: Emergency Medical and Surgical Management
headings.content: Medical intervention for unsafe abortion complications requires a dual approach: stabilizing systemic instability and evacuating the uterus if products of conception are retained. Intravenous access must be secured immediately for fluid resuscitation and administration of broad-spectrum antibiotics to combat pelvic infection. Surgical evacuation, most commonly via Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) or dilation and curettage, is performed to remove retained tissue and stop hemorrhage. In cases of severe uterine perforation or peritonitis, emergency exploratory laparotomy and hysterectomy may become necessary.

headings.title: Post-Abortion Care (PAC) and Counseling
headings.content: Post-Abortion Care is an essential global health strategy designed to manage complications, provide compassionate counseling, and link clients with family planning services. Nurses play a frontline role in delivering non-judgmental care, recognizing that emotional trauma and fear of stigma often accompany physical recovery. Counseling sessions focus on reproductive health education, signs of post-procedure complications, and immediate provision of modern contraceptive methods to prevent recurrent unwanted pregnancies.

headings.title: Preventive Strategies and the Role of the Nurse
headings.content: Prevention remains the most effective intervention against the burden of unsafe abortion. Nurses serve as educators, advocates, and care providers in communities and clinical settings. Key preventive pillars include expanding access to youth-friendly family planning clinics, promoting correct and consistent contraceptive use, and delivering comprehensive sexuality education free from moral judgment. By actively challenging societal stigma and advocating for policy reforms that protect women's health, nurses help bridge the gap between vulnerable populations and safe, accessible reproductive healthcare.
